diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the above construction, we switched between $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}})=0$ for $k$ odd and $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}})=1$ for $k$ even.

There \textbf{are no} learning algorithms (deterministic or probabilistic with success probability $>1/2$) ${\Gamma_n}$ using $\mathcal{T}_\mathbb{N}$ with
$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\!\Gamma_n(F)\!=\!\begin{dcases}
1,\!\!&\text{if $\exists$ a non-trivial eigenfunction},\\
0,\!\!&\text{otherwise},
\end{dcases}\,\, \forall F\!\in\!\Omega_p.
$$

issues.failure_explanation: For any skew-product map $F(x,y)=(x,y+f(x))$ on the torus $[-\pi,\pi]_{\mathrm{per}}^2$, the coordinate $x$ is invariant under $F$. Therefore, any zero-mean function depending only on $x$, such as $g(x,y)=\cos(x)$, lies in $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$ and satisfies $[\mathcal{K}_F g](x,y) = g(x,y+f(x)) = \cos(x) = g(x,y)$. Hence $g$ is an eigenfunction with eigenvalue 1 in $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$, and its spectral measure is a pure atomic measure $\frac{1}{2}\delta_1$, which is not continuous. Thus Lemma B.7(a) is false. Consequently, in the lower bound proofs of Theorem B.8 and Theorem 4, $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}}) = 1$ for all $k$, so the construction never achieves $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}}) = 0$, leaving the lower bound for detecting non-trivial eigenfunctions unproven.

failure_location.quote: If $f$ is strictly increasing on $[-\pi,0]$, the spectral measure of $\mathcal{K}_F$ with respect to any $g\in L^2(\mathcal{X},\omega)$ is continuous on $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$. It follows that there are no eigenfunctions in the subspace $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must construct an adversarial family of smooth measure-preserving maps on the torus where some members are genuinely weakly mixing (possessing no non-trivial eigenfunctions) and others possess non-trivial eigenfunctions, which requires a completely new global proof architecture.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound establishing that determining the existence of non-trivial eigenfunctions (weak mixing) requires at least two limits (i.e., does not belong to $\Delta_2^{\mathbb{P}}$) in Theorem 4 and Theorem B.8 fails, as all maps in the constructed adversarial family possess an infinite-dimensional space of non-trivial eigenfunctions with eigenvalue 1.
issues.title: False absence of non-trivial eigenfunctions in skew-product maps
issues.why_classification: Lemma B.7(a) is mathematically false, and its failure invalidates the lower bound for the decision problem in Theorem 4 and Theorem B.8. Overcoming this requires introducing a new family of smooth, genuinely weakly mixing dynamical systems on the torus, which demands entirely new proof architecture.
